description: Closed-set conformance fixtures for the W1 R0 soc.get_alert_context capability-specific packet, accepted for implementation on 2026-07-26 and not implemented. Positive fixtures must validate, negative-schema fixtures must be rejected structurally, and negative-semantic fixtures must validate structurally while demonstrating a runtime policy violation. The standalone validator independently pins every filename, checks there are no missing/orphan/duplicate fixtures, recomputes every fixture authorization binding against the live schema bytes, recomputes RFC 8785/JCS context digests, and verifies manifest member hashes. This is static evidence only; it proves no endpoint, Fabric grant, W2-F delegation, runtime enforcement or release readiness, and the lifecycle acceptance it carries is a recorded decision rather than evidence.

examples.invariant: TI-3 Fabric tool-grant authority is outside the capability business payload; additionalProperties=false rejects execution_grant.
TI-3 W2-F inference delegation is not Fabric tool authorization; additionalProperties=false rejects delegation_token.
TI-5 The requested SOC alert reference must be digest-bound.
TI-4 Absent, unauthorized and policy-filtered resources share the single generic alert_context_unavailable response code.
TR-1 Actor and tenant are structurally valid but disagree with the credential-derived authorization binding; authorization happens before cache lookup and runtime must reject.

TR-2 Result org_id differs from the credential-derived request authorization binding. include_descendants is pinned const false in C1 v0.1.0, so this witness drifts by org_id alone; runtime must reject rather than widen hierarchy access.
TR-3 Result marking exceeds request clearance on classification and TLP axes; runtime must fail closed.
TR-4 Returned alert digest differs from the digest-pinned request; runtime must reject stale/substituted context.
